outcome: morbidly adherent placenta (placenta accreta vera, increta, percreta)
cohort: 205 pregnant women aged 15-49 years, with pregnancies between 4 and 36 weeks gestation, alive singleton fetus, and history of previous uterine surgery (Caesarean Section, myomectomy, hysterotomy) and/or placenta praevia, excluding those with history of PID, D&C, IUCD insertion, or placenta abruption.
finding: Morbidly adherent placenta (MAP) was found in 9.76% of women with previous uterine scars, with the risk increasing with age, second trimester pregnancy, high parity, previous cesarean section, and shorter duration of the scar.
